_comment: The SCA twin of unsupported-dependency: the same file: path declaration, in the archive the reviewer builds from. The diagnosis does not change - nothing identifies a local path - but this submission is the one npm actually installs from, so its response keeps the lock-file route the XPI branch must not offer, and asks for the library in the archive rather than bundled into the add-on. The committed package-lock.json is not what this fixture is about: a source archive declaring dependencies owes one whatever their source, and a file: spec is skipped by the coverage comparison, so neither lock check speaks here. The XPI here also ships a package.json of its own, which in a source-code submission belongs in the archive - the copy the reviewer reads and the build installs from - so sca-not-required warns that this did not need to be a source submission. It is advice about the NEXT one and narrows nothing here.
